subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we're aligned on Finly's goals and next steps:

Pain points and goals:
- p95 text generation latency target: <= 300ms for single-turn streaming responses (desktop web) across peak hours.
- Streaming UX: must support interleaved partial token updates; client abort/resume behavior important.
- Concurrency: expected 2.5k RPS during peak with average 1.2s token streams per session; spike to 5k RPS for short bursts.
- Current stack: in-house LLM endpoints running on G4dn instances, using batching with custom queueing; observed tail latency spikes and KV cache misses.

Success criteria for POC:
1) Demonstrate p95 <= 300ms for streaming-first flows at 2.5k steady RPS.
2) Keep cost per 1k tokens within 20% of current baseline.
3) No data egress outside US; support VPC peering integration.

Next steps:
- Redwood to run an initial throughput/latency evaluation using representative payloads (we'll use your sample corpus) — target start: Tue 2026-08-11.
- Finly to share sample request traces and representative prompts (Alex / Priya) by EOD Mon 2026-08-10.
- Redwood to provide instrumentation and a short test plan; deliverables: p95 stream latency report, concurrency profile, and a proposed config for Dedicated pool.

I've attached a short snapshot template (finly_p95_snapshot.csv) and our initial proposal (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf).

If any of the items above are off, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise we'll kick off the evaluation tomorrow.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: finly_p95_snapshot.csv, redwood_proposal_v1.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finly.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary.

A few clarifications from our side:
- The 2.5k RPS number is for authenticated web sessions aggregated across our primary region (US-West). Peak bursts to 5k are typically 30–90s and happen ~2x/day.
- Our current p95 baseline for non-streaming calls is ~420ms; streaming UX is currently implemented client-side but we still see partial-update jitter that hurts user perceived latency.
- Security: we can share request traces but will anonymize PII; all traces must remain in the US.

We'll share the sample traces and a set of representative prompts by EOD. Also: two questions for Redwood engineering —
1) Do you have a recommended fallback model variant for lower-cost, higher-availability degradation scenarios?
2) Will the initial evaluation require us to open VPC peering or can you run an ingress-only load generator against our public endpoint?

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency (internal)

Marissa / team — quick internal note:
- We'll spin up a Dedicated test pool that mirrors G4dn-ish throughput characteristics and run both streaming and non-streaming passes.
- Need to confirm whether Finly will open VPC peering for lower variance results; if not, we'll run an ingress-only generator from our test harness (we'll still need sample traces).
- Engineering recommends starting with a 2-node quantized variant + a fallback cheaper model (e.g., 8-bit trimmed variant) to evaluate graceful degradation.

I'll draft the test plan and instrumentation checklist this morning. Who owns file transfer for the traces (Priya / Alex)?

- Aditya
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick turn.

Per Aditya: we'll prepare the Dedicated test pool and test harness. For the two questions you raised:
1) We'll include a recommended fallback model variant in the test report (fast/low-cost quantized variant) and measure user-UX impact during graceful degradation runs.
2) Prefer VPC peering for the most accurate tail-latency measurements — if Finly can open peering we'll coordinate network steps; otherwise we'll proceed with ingress tests and call out the measurement caveats.

I've scheduled a 30-minute sync to kick off the POC and review the test plan on Tue 2026-08-17 16:00 PT. HubSpot link to the deal and calendar invite are here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/DEAL-2026-0091 and the calendar invite should be in your inbox.

Action owners:
- Alex / Priya: upload anonymized traces + sample prompts by EOD Mon 2026-08-10 (Priya please confirm upload method).
- Aditya: share test plan + instrumentation by EOD Tue 2026-08-11.
- Marissa: coordinate Dedicated pool provisioning and send calendar invite.

Talk soon —
